data.title: Tiger Brands Earnings Call Signals Stronger Growth
data.description:
Tiger Brands ((TBLMF)) has held its Q4 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

Tiger Brands delivered a strongly positive earnings call, with management pointing to better margins, returns, volumes, cash generation and brand performance. Investors also heard about consumer pressure, a 19% reported EPS decline, Ingrams execution problems, project delays and volatile commodity conditions, but the operational progress and constructive outlook outweighed these risks.

Transformation Delivers Stronger Returns

Tiger Brands said its two-year transformation has lifted operating margins into double-digit territory, two years ahead of its 2028 target. ROIC has risen from below its cost of capital to more than twice that level, while improved balance-sheet use lifted ROE and market capitalization moved closer to ZAR 40 billion.

Affordability Supports Volume Growth

The affordability strategy helped produce normalized revenue growth of about 3.3% and volume growth of 4.5%. Management said productivity gains were reinvested into lower price points, helping consumers manage inflation while supporting demand for Tiger Brands products.

Underlying Earnings Improve

Underlying HEPS increased 10.5% after removing the noise from the Carozzi transaction. Excluding the effects of gearing and share buybacks, management said growth was closer to 17%, highlighting stronger operating performance beneath the reported figures.

Cost Leadership Expands Margins

Factory efficiencies, continuous improvement, supply-chain optimization and logistics savings supported operating-income growth and margin expansion. Logistics benefits largely offset higher fuel costs during the past six months, allowing Tiger Brands to avoid price increases over that period.

Cash Generation Funds Investment

Cash conversion reached 88% in FY2026, or 94% after adjusting for Carozzi-related taxes that moved into the year. Tiger Brands increased dividends and capital expenditure while generating strong cash, and said buybacks since FY2024 created a ZAR 1.63 per-share benefit.

Portfolio Simplification Continues

Management said the group has exited unwanted or underperforming activities, optimized its balance sheet and returned capital to shareholders. Chococam is the only major outstanding portfolio transaction, with its resolution dependent on the tax situation in Cameroon.

International Markets Gain Momentum

International operations delivered strong growth and a material improvement in profitability, helped by distributors and expansion into neighboring, West African and East African markets. Crosse & Blackwell was named Mozambique’s favorite mayonnaise, while Benny and Jolly Jus were highlighted as products with export potential.

Factories Show Operational Progress

Manufacturing performance improved, with better factory efficiency, product quality, customer complaints and lost-time injury measures. In baking, complaints were at an all-time low, while Digibake technology monitored bread weight, line speed and damaged loaves across production lines.

Digital Strategy Targets Efficiency

The Board approved Tiger Brands’ digital transformation strategy and created a committee to identify opportunities across the value chain. Plans include a supply-chain control tower, human-capital software, demand and production tools, stronger cybersecurity and a Data Lake to improve decision-making.

Capital Spending Rises

Capital expenditure increased to approximately ZAR 1.7 billion in FY2026 from about ZAR 1.2 billion previously. Spending is focused on automation, efficiency and major projects such as the Paarl mega site, Super Bakery and a mega distribution center.

Baking Focuses on Market Share

Baking reported normalized operating-income growth and margin expansion, supported by better channel mix, lower conversion costs, fewer damages and improved maintenance. Tiger Brands is investing behind pricing and market-share gains, with further manufacturing benefits expected once the Super Bakery is operational.

Grains Posts Another Strong Year

Grains delivered a third consecutive strong year, supported by Tastic, supply-chain scale, stock management and soft-commodity deflation, particularly in rice. Jungle volumes and margins improved after a summer campaign, King Foods turned around and the portfolio became less dependent on rice.

Jungle Expands Breakfast Innovation

Jungle has launched three ready-to-eat cereal variants and cornflakes as it seeks to capture more of the breakfast market. Management said the portfolio is benefiting from the gap left by ProNutro’s exit and believes Jungle has substantial room to grow.

Culinary Builds on Brand Strength

Culinary continued to beat expectations through affordability initiatives, continuous improvement and strong brands. Margin gains came from value engineering, recipe and packaging changes, vinegar insourcing and Mrs. Ball’s production, while the pipeline includes brand tiering, Black Cat Creamia and lower-oil Kasi mayonnaise.

Snacks and Beverages Offer Potential

After exiting Beacon, Tiger Brands is concentrating on the more profitable parts of its snacks and treats portfolio, with Jungle reaching the number-three position by count line. Energade and Oros gained share, while site consolidation and a beverage distribution center should improve efficiency.

Home Care Remains a Bright Spot

Home Care delivered an exceptional result, with Doom retaining leadership in pesticides and the Dyroach and Dyant migration into Doom Pro performing well. Jeyes Thick Bleach gained share, supported by investment to insource production and product registrations that can reduce reliance on South African seasonality.

Sustainability Supports Business Value

Management said sustainability is being built into business cases where it can reduce costs or improve efficiency. Initiatives include local agricultural sourcing, solar power, lower landfill use, water efficiency and Black farmer development, while the Langeberg & Ashton transaction created a trust for the Ashton community.

Brands Support Export Growth

Tiger Brands said most of its products hold the number-one position in their categories, including culinary brands, Maynards, Oros and Energade. Export growth is being pursued through neighboring markets and distributors while the group continues to manufacture mainly in South Africa.

People and Sourcing Gain Attention

About 160 people who had previously left the company returned during the past two years, reflecting improved culture and skills development. Since roughly 80% of the business processes agricultural products, management is also prioritizing training, sustainable sourcing and alternative supply-chain options.

Reported EPS Falls on Comparisons

Reported EPS declined 19%, mainly because the prior year included proceeds from the Carozzi disposal and the Baby Wellbeing transaction. Management contrasted that decline with the stronger normalized HEPS result, which better reflects ongoing operations.

Consumers and Retailers Remain Pressured

Lower-income consumers are facing higher fuel and taxi costs and less disposable income, leading to smaller baskets and greater demand for value. Retailers and wholesalers are also dealing with rising costs, margin pressure and relatively flat food-market turnover.

Promotions Increase Margin Pressure

Promotions account for more than half of sales at many retailers and as much as 70% to 80% in some categories. That environment makes pricing, margin protection and product profitability increasingly important for Tiger Brands and its customers.

Ingrams Relaunch Faces Setback

The Ingrams relaunch was the main disappointment in Home and Personal Care after supplier and production problems caused stock-outs and poor timing. The business margin fell to about 18%, although management said the operational issues have been resolved and another relaunch is planned.

Super Bakery Runs Behind Schedule

The Super Bakery project is several months late because of regulatory and planning approvals, including new height restrictions affecting silo construction. Management said it remains within budget, while the delay provides additional time to optimize existing Gauteng bakeries.

Grains Margins May Normalize

Management cautioned that the 19% second-half grains margin is unlikely to be sustainable. The strong result benefited partly from soft-commodity and rice deflation, even though the grains team has exceeded expectations for three consecutive years.

Destocking Weighs on General Trade

March-to-March trading conditions triggered destocking and added pressure in the second half, with recovery typically taking six to eight months. Some customers may not return to former inventory levels, as concerns about looting and property damage continue to make them cautious.

Food Inflation Risks Return

Tiger Brands expects food inflation to return as oil prices lift diesel and fertilizer costs and maize and global rice prices rise. Management also pointed to El Niño risks, including the possibility that farmers may plant 5% to 10% fewer hectares of maize.

External Volatility Remains High

The group continues to manage volatility in oil prices, climate conditions, geopolitical conflict, supply chains and cybersecurity. Recent Johannesburg flooding, drought conditions, difficulties tracking imported goods and data-protection risks underline the need for continued operational vigilance.

Beverage Pricing Weighs on Margins

Beverage margins declined in the second half as Tiger Brands invested in lower price points to respond to carbonated-drink competition and private-label squashes. The strategy helped Energade and Oros gain market share, but came at a near-term profitability cost.

Wheat Exposure Requires Discipline

Wheat deflation supported milling and baking margins, but management said the largest improvement came from disposing of the unprofitable Randfontein wheat operations. The remaining business still faces agricultural sourcing and wheat-market issues, including calls for more efficient local farming and stronger protection.

Guidance Points to Steady Expansion

Management expects short- to medium-term volume growth of 1% to 3%, with longer-term growth ahead of GDP, while near-term revenue should grow slightly faster than inflation. Operating margin has room to move toward 15% and stay above it, working capital is guided at 45 to 65 days, gearing is moving toward 1.0 times EBITDA from 0.4 times, and capital expenditure should remain near ZAR 2 billion for another year or two before easing to ZAR 1.2 billion to ZAR 1.5 billion.

Tiger Brands’ earnings call showed a business with stronger foundations, better execution and a healthier return profile. Although consumer weakness, commodity risks and a few operational setbacks remain, management’s volume strategy, investment pipeline and margin ambitions leave the overall outlook constructive for investors.

data.title: Natural Resource Partners Earnings Call Signals Strength and Challenges
data.description:
Natural Resource Partners ((NRP)) has held its Q3 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

Natural Resource Partners delivered a broadly positive third quarter, supported by strong free cash flow, major debt repayment and a much larger distribution. Still, management pointed to weak coal markets and a prolonged soda ash downturn, with lower earnings, suspended Sisecam Wyoming distributions and a tougher outlook for 2027.

Free Cash Flow Supported a Larger Distribution

NRP generated $45 million of free cash flow in the third quarter and $166 million over the last 12 months before its soda ash investment. The partnership raised its distribution to $2.34 per common unit from $0.75 in the second quarter as it began paying out cash beyond unit-holder tax liabilities.

Debt Reduction Strengthened the Balance Sheet

NRP paid down $13 million of debt during the quarter and fully repaid the remaining balance on its $13 million Opco Credit Facility. Just $14 million of debt remains to be repaid next month, reducing interest costs and improving corporate and financing results.

Mineral Rights Remained a Strong Cash Generator

The Mineral Rights segment produced $37 million of net income, $46 million of operating cash flow and $47 million of free cash flow in the third quarter. Over the last 12 months, the segment generated $185 million of free cash flow, reinforcing its importance to NRP’s finances.

Higher Metallurgical Coal Prices Lifted Cash Flow

Mineral Rights operating and free cash flow each rose by $2 million from the prior-year quarter. Higher metallurgical coal prices and volumes at certain properties, along with payment timing, more than offset the absence of lease amendment fees received in the prior-year period.

Metallurgical Coal Drove Royalty Revenue

Metallurgical coal represented about 70% of coal royalty revenue and 45% of coal royalty sales volumes in the third quarter. Mineral Rights net income nevertheless fell by $4 million year over year, mainly because of higher depreciation, depletion and amortization expense.

Lower Interest Costs Improved Corporate Results

Corporate and financing net income, operating cash flow and free cash flow each improved by $1 million from a year earlier. The gains reflected lower debt, reduced interest costs and less cash paid for interest after NRP’s balance-sheet reductions.

Soda Ash Asset Retains Long-Term Appeal

Management described the Sisecam Wyoming investment as one of the world’s lowest-cost soda ash operations. Its managing partner is pursuing cost savings while maintaining safe, reliable operations and protecting the plant’s competitive position.

Market Downturn Weighed on Soda Ash Earnings

The soda ash market remains oversupplied, with too much production and weak demand. Rising natural soda ash exports from China are pressuring older synthetic plants to modernize, close or take both steps.

Soda Ash Prices and Earnings Declined

Soda ash segment net income decreased by $2 million from the prior-year quarter. Lower international selling prices and weaker flat-glass demand drove the decline, although international prices have stopped falling and remain below most producers’ costs.

Domestic Soda Ash Outlook Is More Difficult

Management expects domestic prices to decline as contracts reset and the premium over international prices narrows. It said 2027 will be harder than 2026, while market closures are progressing slowly and rebalancing is likely to take years rather than quarters.

Sisecam Distributions Remain Suspended

Soda ash operating and free cash flow were flat because NRP received no distribution from Sisecam Wyoming in either the third quarter of 2025 or 2026. Payments are not expected to resume until demand improves or the market sees a significant supply response.

Coal Markets Face Several Pressures

Weak global steel demand continues to limit metallurgical coal prices, while cheap natural gas and high power-plant inventories weigh on thermal coal. Management said it sees no clear development that would change those conditions, and diesel prices have risen more than 75% this year, squeezing operator margins.

Renewable Projects Remain on the Agenda

NRP said its work involving carbon dioxide sequestration, solar, geothermal and other alternative uses is unchanged after the debt reduction and revised cash allocation strategy. The partnership continues to seek lessees to develop projects across its acreage.

Capital Allocation Will Remain Flexible

The board will review distributions every quarter based on results, liquidity needs and other uses of cash, including unit repurchases or opportunistic acquisitions. If NRP retains cash, management said it would seek more than a dollar of intrinsic value per unit for every dollar kept.

Forward Guidance Points to Higher Payouts but Tougher Markets

NRP raised the third-quarter distribution to $2.34 per unit after generating $45 million of free cash flow, paying down $13 million of debt and making $32 million available for distribution. Future payouts remain subject to quarterly board decisions, while management sees no material coal-price change for 2027 and expects lower domestic soda ash prices, delayed Sisecam payments and a multiyear market recovery.

The earnings call showed a financially stronger NRP with robust cash generation, lower debt and a significantly higher distribution. However, weak coal fundamentals and a prolonged soda ash oversupply will test results, making disciplined capital allocation and the strength of the Mineral Rights portfolio central to the investment case.

data.title: Intact Financial Earnings Call Signals Broad Strength
data.description:
Intact Financial ((TSE:IFC)) has held its Q3 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

Intact Financial’s earnings call conveyed strong confidence, with management highlighting sustained returns, disciplined underwriting, growing investment and distribution income, and a solid capital position. Catastrophe losses, personal property weakness, UK&I costs, U.S. pricing pressure and excess capital weighed on results, but the positive developments clearly outweighed the challenges.

Strong Third-Quarter Earnings and Operating Return

Intact reported net operating income per share of $3.63, its second-highest third-quarter result, while the combined ratio improved to 94% and the top line grew 5%. Operating ROE reached 16%, marking the company’s tenth straight quarter above 15%.

Book Value Continued to Expand

Book value per share rose 8% year over year to $111.11. Growth reached double digits when accumulated other comprehensive income was excluded, underscoring the company’s continued ability to build shareholder value.

Personal Auto Growth and Profitability

Canadian personal auto premiums increased 10%, including 2 percentage points from unit growth, while the combined ratio was 91.2%. This result came despite catastrophe losses nearly 2 points higher than last year, and premium growth has exceeded the industry for seven consecutive quarters.

Personal Auto Outlook Remains Positive

Management expects Canadian personal auto growth to continue outperforming the industry while keeping the combined ratio near current levels. Industry growth is expected to remain in the mid-single-digit range over the next 12 months.

Personal Property Underlying Results Improved

Personal property premiums grew 7% in the quarter, including 1 point from unit growth, but the combined ratio reached 105% after 33 points of catastrophe losses. Underlying performance continued to improve, with the past-12-month home insurance combined ratio at 92.5%, consistent with the company’s sub-95% guidance.

Hard Personal Property Market Supports Share Gains

Intact expects hard market conditions in personal property to persist over the next 12 months. Management said the company is well positioned to keep gaining market share as pricing and underwriting conditions remain favorable.

Canadian Commercial Lines Gained Momentum

Canadian commercial premium growth improved sequentially to 2%, including 4 points from higher units and rates, partly offset by a shift toward smaller accounts. Submissions rose close to 10%, and management expects the business to outperform industry growth over the next year.

Commercial Underwriting Stayed Profitable

The Canadian commercial combined ratio was 91.9%, despite catastrophe losses running 7 points above expectations. Excluding catastrophes, the ratio was 85%, in line with the five-year average, while management continued to target a low-90s ratio or better.

Stable Conditions in SME Commercial Lines

Retentions in Canadian small and medium-sized enterprise and mid-market business remained above 90%, while price changes were close to the mid-single digits. Rates plus exposure also stayed in the mid-single-digit range, with these segments representing roughly 80% or more of Canadian commercial lines.

U.S. Underwriting Continued to Outperform

U.S. growth was 3%, driven by expansion in the company’s strongest verticals, while about two-thirds of the portfolio operated below an 85% combined ratio. The overall ratio was 85.2%, extending the company’s streak below 90% to 13 quarters and its outperformance versus the industry to 18 quarters.

U.S. Growth and Margins Have Room to Improve

Intact expects the U.S. combined ratio to remain below 90% over the next year. Top-line growth is expected to gain momentum through profitable verticals, geographic expansion and offerings including fine arts, U.S. construction liability and excess and surplus casualty coverage.

UK&I Underwriting Action Plan Targets Improvement

The UK&I combined ratio was 94.1%, broadly matching the current run rate. Management is pursuing a path toward a ratio near 90% through artificial intelligence pricing and risk models, technology modernization, legacy-system retirement and productivity gains.

Underlying Loss Performance Remained Solid

The consolidated underlying current accident-year loss ratio was 55.4%. Favorable prior-year development added 6 points during the quarter, roughly matching the average contribution over the past two years and remaining broadly consistent with the second quarter.

Investment Income Benefited from Higher Yields

Operating net investment income rose 5% to $422 million as assets grew and yields increased. The 4.6% reinvestment yield was 50 basis points above the portfolio book yield, supporting expectations for net investment income above $1.7 billion in 2026 and $1.8 billion in 2027.

Distribution Income and On Side Expanded

Distribution income increased 16% year over year to $171 million, helped by organic growth and improved margins at BrokerLink. On Side revenue rose more than 30% following recent catastrophe events, while management maintained its long-term expectation for 10% annual distribution-income growth.

Capital Strength Supported Buybacks

Adjusted debt represented 16.3% of total capital, while the total capital margin stood at $3.6 billion. Intact repurchased about $200 million of shares during the quarter, bringing buybacks over the past 12 months close to $600 million.

Long-Term Financial Targets Were Exceeded

Intact said it exceeded its goal of outperforming industry ROE by at least 500 basis points, delivering 740 basis points of outperformance in 2025 and an average close to 700 basis points over five and 10 years. Net operating income per share compounded at 14% over five years and 12% over 10 years, ahead of the 10% target.

AI Has Become a Significant Earnings Driver

The company now has more than 600 AI specialists and over 600 proprietary models in production across Canada, the U.S. and UK&I. Machine learning supports pricing for 94% of Canadian personal lines and 75% of Canadian commercial lines, generating nearly $250 million in recurring pretax earnings.

AI Investment Could Improve Loss and Expense Ratios

Management expects AI-related recurring pretax earnings to double within 24 months as investment continues in pricing, risk selection, customer service, software and efficiency. About 60% of the expected increase is projected to come through the loss ratio, with the remainder benefiting the expense ratio.

Claims and Supply Chain Capabilities Add Value

Intact handles more than 95% of claims internally, giving it control over claims management, fraud detection, repairs and supply chains. Management said these capabilities help close files faster and reduce leakage in indemnity payments.

Alberta Reform Could Improve Auto Economics

Management said Alberta’s Care-First reform should lower costs on new claims beginning January 1 and produce negative year-over-year claim-cost inflation in the province. The reform is intended to restore sustainability after the industry lost nearly $1 billion in Alberta over the past two years.

Brands and Distribution Channels Remain Strong

Intact owns Canada’s number-one and number-three insurance brands, and said three out of four customers are advocates. Its widely downloaded insurance app, broker network, direct-to-consumer platform and agency channels provide flexibility in how customers interact with the company.

Catastrophe Losses Exceeded Expectations

Catastrophe losses reached $660 million in the quarter, 4 points above expectations. Over the past 12 months, catastrophe losses have been close to the company’s $1.2 billion annual guidance, keeping weather-related volatility a key risk for investors.

Personal Property Posted a Quarterly Loss

Personal property reported a 105% combined ratio for the quarter, including 33 points from catastrophe losses. The result highlights the impact of severe events even as the underlying home insurance trend continued to improve.

UK&I Top-Line Growth Was Uneven

UK&I top-line growth was flat during the quarter, and management expects quarterly performance to remain uneven over the next year. The integration of NIG, new pricing models in a competitive market, and variability in specialty and London market business are expected to create volatility.

UK&I Technology Costs Will Take Time to Decline

The UK&I expense ratio remains about 3 points above peers, with technology costs elevated while policies move from legacy systems to new platforms. Management expects the technology conversion process to take approximately 24 to 36 months before the full benefits are visible.

Consolidated Expenses Remain at the High End

The consolidated expense ratio was 33.9%, a modest improvement from a year earlier. However, management expects the full-year 2026 ratio to be at the higher end of its 33% to 34% range.

Large U.S. Property Accounts Faced Pricing Pressure

Prices in U.S. special property and large property accounts declined by double digits, prompting Intact to shrink a portfolio it still views as attractive. This pressure contributed to U.S. top-line growth of only about 3% in the quarter.

Excess Capital Reduced Reported ROE

Operating ROE of 16% included an estimated 2-point drag from excess capital. Management said retaining capital for strategic flexibility reduces current ROE, particularly as it considers potentially larger merger and acquisition opportunities.

Alberta Outlook Changed Because of Legacy Claims

The Alberta reform is expected to create a one-time impact in 2027 and led Intact to modify its outlook. Existing prior claims are long-tail liabilities, with a weighted-average cash-flow duration of approximately three to four years.

Canadian Auto Industry Still Faces Cost Pressure

The Canadian auto industry continues to face mid-single-digit physical-damage inflation and very high bodily-injury-liability inflation. Management noted that these pressures contributed to industry losses of nearly $1 billion in Alberta over the past two years before the Care-First reform.

M&A Plans Compete with Share Repurchases

Intact is balancing continued buybacks with the need to preserve capital for possible acquisitions. Management said transactions exceeding $15 billion could require substantial equity financing and reduce the capital available for more aggressive repurchases.

Forward Guidance Points to Continued Earnings Growth

Management expects Canadian personal auto industry growth in the mid-single digits, with Intact outperforming and maintaining its current combined ratio, while personal property remains below 95% and Canadian commercial lines deliver a low-90s ratio or better. U.S. margins are expected to stay below 90%, UK&I growth should be uneven as its ratio moves toward 90%, and 2027 is expected to improve over 2026.

The company also expects 2026 consolidated expenses near the high end of 33% to 34%, investment income above $1.7 billion before rising above $1.8 billion in 2027, and distribution income to grow 10% annually over time. AI-related recurring pretax earnings are expected to double to about $500 million within 24 months, while Intact continues targeting annual ROE outperformance of at least 500 basis points and 10% long-term growth in net operating income per share.

Overall, Intact’s earnings call showed a business delivering strong returns, resilient underwriting and growing technology-driven advantages. Catastrophe volatility, UK&I execution costs, large-account pricing pressure and capital allocation choices remain watch points, but management’s confidence in the company’s earnings power and long-term growth strategy was clear.

data.title: AstraZeneca Earnings Call Highlights Growth and Pipeline Strength
data.description:
AstraZeneca plc ((GB:AZN)) has held its Q3 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

AstraZeneca’s earnings call carried a strongly positive tone, with broad revenue growth, strong pipeline progress and multiple new approvals reinforcing confidence in its long-term expansion plans. Management also acknowledged patent losses, generic competition, higher investment, restructuring costs and weaker cash flow, but presented these pressures as manageable within a broader growth strategy.

Revenue and Earnings Growth

AstraZeneca reported 7% revenue growth and 14% core EPS growth for the first nine months of 2026. Excluding Farxiga and Brilinta, revenue increased 12%, highlighting the strength of the wider portfolio.

Pipeline Delivery and New Approvals

The company reported positive results from 12 Phase III programs and received first approvals for four new medicines, including Etcamah in the U.S. AstraZeneca now has 14 approved new molecular entities toward its goal of delivering 20 by 2030.

More Than $10 Billion in Phase III Potential

The 12 positive Phase III readouts represent more than $10 billion in non-risk-adjusted peak-year sales potential. Management said the data have reduced development risk and strengthened confidence in its $80 billion 2030 ambition.

Broad Therapy and Geographic Growth

Oncology, rare disease, and respiratory and immunology each delivered double-digit growth during the first nine months. The U.S., Europe, and emerging markets outside China also recorded robust expansion.

China Growth Despite Procurement Pressure

China continued to face volume-based procurement pressure, but revenue grew 13% when that impact was excluded. Underlying growth in Farxiga, roxadustat, and Lynparza was also described as being at the strong 15% level.

Alliance Revenue Accelerated

Alliance revenue increased 32% in the first nine months, supported by higher profit sales from Enhertu, Datroway, and Tezspire. The growth mainly reflected markets where AstraZeneca’s partners record product sales.

Margins and Full-Year Expectations

Core gross margin was 83% in the first nine months, and AstraZeneca maintained its full-year outlook. Management expects revenue growth in the mid- to high-single-digit range and core EPS growth in the low double digits.

Investment in the Growth Pipeline

Core research and development spending rose 5% and represented 23% of revenue. AstraZeneca is investing in bispecifics, cell therapies, T-cell engagers, weight management, and cardiovascular outcome trials.

Reshaping Program Targets Savings

The three-year Reshaping for Sustainable Growth program will redeploy resources and strengthen capabilities across the business. It is designed to produce $1.5 billion in annualized pretax run-rate benefits, with activities expected to be completed by the end of 2029.

Oncology Revenue Growth

Oncology revenue increased 16% to $21.9 billion in the first nine months, including 17% growth in the third quarter. Growth was double digit across major regions, led by an 18% increase in the U.S.

Tagrisso Surpassed $2 Billion

Tagrisso generated $2.1 billion in third-quarter revenue, up 12% year over year and above $2 billion for the first time. Demand was broad across indications and regions, while FLAURA2 retained a leading position in major markets.

Imfinzi and Imjudo Momentum

Imfinzi revenue grew 26% and Imjudo revenue rose 25% in the third quarter. Combined revenue from the two medicines exceeded $2 billion for the first time, supported by established uses and newer launches.

Calquence and Enhertu Expanded

Calquence revenue increased 16% to $1.1 billion and became the leading BTK inhibitor in first-line CLL across the top eight markets. Enhertu revenue rose 35% to $969 million, including almost 50% growth in the U.S.

New Oncology Launches Progressed

Truqap revenue rose 9% to $210 million, while Datroway generated $78 million from uptake in lung and breast cancer. Etcamah showed encouraging early launch signals, and Zegfrovy recorded its first revenue ahead of its U.S. launch.

Positive Oncology Phase III Data

The SAFFRON trial reduced the risk of death by 32% compared with platinum chemotherapy and extended median overall survival by nearly five months in selected patients. SANOVO extended median progression-free survival beyond two years and improved median overall survival by 9.6 months.

Additional Oncology Breakthroughs

DESTINY-Lung04, DeLLphi-305, VOLGA, and CLARITY-Gastric01 each produced important efficacy results across lung, ovarian, and gastric cancers. The studies showed stronger survival, response, or recurrence outcomes that further broaden AstraZeneca’s oncology opportunities.

ADC and Immuno-Oncology Platforms

AstraZeneca entered an equity investment and clinical collaboration with Summit Therapeutics involving ivonescimab, sone-ve, and Datroway. The company now has 15 Phase III trials for next-generation immuno-oncology bispecifics across nine tumor types.

Respiratory and Immunology Growth

Respiratory and immunology revenue rose 11% to $2.5 billion in the third quarter. Fasenra, Tezspire, Breztri, and Saphnelo grew 14%, 51%, 14%, and 32%, respectively.

Tozorakimab COPD Results

Tozorakimab reduced COPD exacerbations across patient groups, with the largest reduction reaching 43% among patients with higher eosinophil counts. Benefits were also observed among former smokers and across the overall population.

Tezspire Eosinophilic Esophagitis Data

Both Tezspire doses produced statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvements in histologic remission and swallowing symptoms in the CROSSING trial. Benefits continued through week 52, with about one-third of patients achieving total endoscopic remission.

Rare Disease Revenue Growth

Rare disease revenue increased 11% in the first nine months to $7.5 billion, supported by double-digit growth across key medicines. Ultomiris revenue rose 19% in the third quarter, while Strensiq grew 34%.

Rare Disease Launch Opportunities

Ultomiris received accelerated U.S. approval in IgA nephropathy, while Klygefa and Amlypave gained approvals in Japan. Efzimfotase alfa was filed across major markets and received U.S. priority review.

Efzimfotase Alfa and Cliramitug Potential

Management sees efzimfotase alfa as capable of reaching more patients through less frequent, lower-volume dosing and wider disease coverage. Cliramitug is being evaluated in ATTR cardiomyopathy and was described as another substantial commercial opportunity.

Weight Management and Cardiovascular Research

Phase III studies are ongoing for elecoglipron, and AstraZeneca started three Phase III trials for lenbelintide. The company is also advancing laroprovstat monotherapy and fixed-dose combinations with rosuvastatin.

Cell Therapy and T-Cell Engagers

AstraZeneca has three Phase III trials of AZD0120 in multiple myeloma and two Phase III trials of surovatamig in B-cell lymphomas. Four additional cell therapies and four T-cell engagers are in early clinical development.

Large 2027 Pipeline Catalyst Set

The company expects more than 20 key Phase III readouts in 2027, including pivotal data for nine potential new medicines. These programs represent more than $20 billion in non-risk-adjusted peak-year revenue potential.

Balance Sheet Remained Strong

Operating cash flow was $10.9 billion in the first nine months, and management said it remained comfortable with current gross debt. Net debt to EBITDA stood at 1.2 times.

New Strategic R&D Center

AstraZeneca officially opened a strategic research and development center in Kendall Square, Massachusetts. The site strengthens the company’s presence in the Greater Boston life sciences ecosystem.

Biopharmaceuticals Revenue Declined

Biopharmaceuticals revenue fell 6% to $5.6 billion in the third quarter. Growth in respiratory and immunology was not enough to offset expected pressure from Farxiga, Brilinta, and roxadustat.

CVRM Faced Exclusivity Pressure

Cardiovascular, renal, and metabolism revenue declined 18% to $2.6 billion. Farxiga revenue fell 23% to $1.6 billion because of U.S. loss of exclusivity and volume-based procurement in China.

Symbicort Sales Declined

Symbicort revenue dropped 11% to $660 million, with U.S. sales down 25% after a second generic competitor entered the market. China continued to provide growth for the medicine.

Soliris Continued to Contract

Soliris revenue continued to decline as patients switched to Ultomiris and biosimilar competition increased. The shift reflects the ongoing transition within AstraZeneca’s complement franchise.

Delayed Graft Function Program Ended

AstraZeneca discontinued Ultomiris development in delayed graft function after the program failed to show consistent efficacy. The company said this setback did not alter the broader value of its pipeline.

Operating Cash Flow Was Lower

Operating cash flow of $10.9 billion was below the comparative period. Management attributed the decline to a prior-year Lynparza milestone and working-capital effects linked to Farxiga’s U.S. exclusivity loss.

Capital and Deal Payments Increased

Capital expenditure reached $2.3 billion in the first nine months, while deal-related payments totaled $4.3 billion. The payments included the Dizal collaboration and milestones from earlier business-development transactions.

Restructuring Costs Will Be Significant

The reshaping program is expected to incur up to $2 billion in one-time restructuring costs. Management described the amount primarily as a cash cost spread over the program period as resources are redeployed.

Fourth-Quarter Expense Pressures

AstraZeneca expects second-half gross margin to be below the first half because of the seasonal mix of lower-margin medicines. Fourth-quarter costs are also expected to rise because of operating expenses, China-related items, higher bond interest, lease expenses, and a Summit-related charge.

Competitive Headwinds Persist

Management highlighted generic competition in several markets and noted that Calquence enters the U.S. IRA framework in 2027. China also remains highly competitive, particularly in oncology, alongside the continuing impact of volume-based procurement.

Clinical Setbacks Were Absorbed

Management acknowledged market attention on the Wainua and SERENA-4 study failures. It said that, on a net present value basis, the overall value of the readouts increased after those setbacks were weighed against the positive results.

Full-Year Guidance

AstraZeneca maintained its expectations for mid- to high-single-digit revenue growth, low-double-digit core EPS growth, and a core gross margin stable to slightly above 2025 levels. R&D spending is expected at the upper end of the low-20s percentage range, while the core tax rate is forecast at 18% to 22%.

The company expects capital expenditure to rise by a low-teens percentage compared with 2025, with about $2.5 billion of milestone payments from earlier transactions. Fourth-quarter operating and finance expenses are expected to increase, while the reshaping program could generate $1.5 billion in annualized benefits after up to $2 billion in one-time costs.

AstraZeneca’s 2027 pipeline remains a major catalyst, with more than 20 high-value trial readouts and pivotal data for nine potential new medicines. Together, these programs represent more than $20 billion in non-risk-adjusted peak-year revenue potential.

AstraZeneca’s earnings call showed a company balancing near-term patent and cost pressures with strong commercial execution and an increasingly valuable pipeline. The breadth of growth across oncology, rare disease, respiratory medicine, and emerging therapies supported management’s confidence in continued expansion.

The overall message for investors was positive: current challenges are real, but AstraZeneca believes its launches, clinical successes, and 2027 catalysts can sustain growth through the decade.

data.title: Ørsted Earnings Call Highlights Growth Amid Key Risks
data.description:
Orsted ((DK:ORSTED)) has held its Q3 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

Ørsted’s earnings call carried a predominantly positive tone, with management highlighting stronger earnings, progress across its offshore construction portfolio and improving regulatory conditions. Those gains were tempered by a DKK 3.4 billion noncash impairment, higher net debt, weaker returns on capital, increased employee injuries and unresolved transaction and tax-equity steps.

European Offshore Wind Rules Improve

Regulatory frameworks for future offshore wind projects are improving across Denmark, the U.K., Poland, Belgium and the Netherlands. Germany approved a draft amendment introducing contracts for difference, although Ørsted said an initial merchant phase before a CfD would be unnecessary.

Large Auction Pipeline Ahead

More than 15 gigawatts of new offshore capacity is expected to be auctioned in core markets in 2027. Nearly all of those markets have also committed to further auction rounds between 2028 and 2030, supporting Ørsted’s longer-term growth outlook.

1.6 Gigawatts Commissioned

Borkum Riffgrund 3 in Germany and Revolution Wind in the United States entered commercial operations. Together, the projects add 1.6 gigawatts of commissioned offshore wind capacity to Ørsted’s operating base.

Strategic Priorities Advance

Management said it made substantial progress on strengthening the capital structure, completing its offshore construction portfolio and improving competitiveness. All projects under construction were described as progressing according to plan and budget, while capital allocation remained disciplined.

Divestment and Tax Risks Ease

Ørsted’s divestment program now has only the sale of its 55% stake in Greater Changhua 2 outstanding. A favorable final tax opinion on Walney Extension and Hornsea 1, together with the Elsam case, was described as an important step in reducing balance-sheet risk.

U.S. Onshore Platform Remains Strong

Ørsted said its U.S. onshore business continues to benefit from strong market fundamentals. The business has more than 6 gigawatts of equipment secured for tax credits, strengthening its development pipeline.

Blackwater Solar Construction Begins

Construction started on the 200-megawatt Blackwater Solar project in New Mexico. Ørsted expects the project to enter commercial operations in the second half of 2027, adding to its U.S. renewable portfolio.

Gunfleet Sands Stake Acquired

Ørsted exercised its buyback right to acquire the remaining stake in the U.K.’s Gunfleet Sands 1 and 2 projects for about GBP 15 million. Full ownership gives the company more flexibility to assess potential lifetime extensions.

Nine-Month EBITDA Rises Nearly 20%

EBITDA excluding new partnerships and cancellation fees exceeded DKK 20 billion in the first nine months, up nearly 20% from a year earlier. Growth reflected ramping offshore generation, slightly stronger wind speeds and higher power prices.

Borkum Riffgrund 3 Starts Operations

The 913-megawatt Borkum Riffgrund 3 wind farm entered commercial operations in August. It is one of Germany’s largest operating offshore wind farms and gives Ørsted six operational projects in the German North Sea.

Revolution Wind Goes Commercial

Revolution Wind completed installation of its remaining turbines and began commercial operations under power purchase agreements with Rhode Island and Connecticut. The project is expected to generate enough electricity for more than 350,000 homes and businesses.

Greater Changhua Nears Completion

All 66 turbines at Greater Changhua 2b and 4 have delivered first power, with only two still awaiting commissioning. The export cable for Greater Changhua 2b was completed, and full commissioning is expected in the fourth quarter.

Baltica 2 Construction Advances

Ørsted completed installation of all 111 monopile foundations at Baltica 2, including those for four offshore substations. Project completion reached about 45%, up from 40% in the prior quarter, while two of four export cables were ready for transport to the site.

Sunrise Wind Moves Forward

Sunrise Wind reached approximately 60% completion, compared with 50% in the second quarter. Foundation installation was complete, while 31 of 84 turbines and 78 array cables had been installed, keeping the project on track for planned commissioning.

Hornsea 3 Progresses Toward Grid Connection

Hornsea 3 reached about 40% completion, up from 30% in the second quarter. Ørsted installed the second offshore converter station, completed 95 of 197 turbine foundations and secured an initial grid connection.

Hornsea 3 Battery Enters Testing

Construction of the 300-megawatt battery system at Hornsea 3’s onshore converter station has been completed. Described as one of Europe’s largest, the battery is now entering its testing phase.

Offshore EBITDA Jumps 68%

Third-quarter offshore earnings rose 68% year over year to DKK 3.7 billion, with every subsegment improving. The increase reflected ramp-up at Greater Changhua 2b and 4 and Revolution Wind, stronger wind speeds, higher power prices and better trading contributions.

Onshore and Bioenergy Earnings Improve

Onshore earnings increased 24% to DKK 1 billion, helped by new Badger Wind generation and higher wind speeds. Bioenergy and Other earnings rose to DKK 400 million from a DKK 100 million loss, supported by higher power prices and stronger condensing generation.

Adjusted Profit Returns to Positive

Net profit adjusted for impairments, new partnership fees and cancellation fees reached DKK 2.2 billion in the third quarter. That compared with a DKK 400 million adjusted loss in the same period last year.

Liquidity and Credit Metrics Stay Strong

Funds from operations to adjusted net debt stood at about 37%, above Ørsted’s target of more than 30%. Liquidity reserves exceeded DKK 105 billion, while more than 90% of gross debt was fixed-rate, with an average modified duration of around five years.

Tax-Credit Monetization Advances

Ørsted said the Revolution Wind tax-credit process was slightly more positive than at the start of the year, with companies signing up. The additional 10% community tax credit was confirmed, while Sunrise Wind tax-equity structuring was progressing as expected.

Growth Will Favor Value Over Volume

Management reiterated that investment decisions will prioritize value rather than capacity growth. Ørsted uses partnerships, project-level financing and other tools to manage future project and farm-down risks, while targeting a 150-to-300-basis-point minimum spread to its cost of capital.

Long-Term Growth Outlook Remains Positive

Management pointed to EBITDA of about DKK 25 billion last year, more than DKK 28 billion expected for 2026 and above DKK 32 billion in the following year. Growth is expected to slow between 2028 and 2030, but Ørsted still sees itself as a net growth company in the 2030s.

Employee Injury Rate Increases

Ørsted’s total recordable injury rate rose in the first nine months compared with the same period last year. The increase was mainly linked to incidents involving its own employees, while contractor incidents and contractor hours both declined.

Greater Changhua Reports Turbine Incidents

Greater Changhua 2b and 4 experienced separate thermal and blade incidents at two commissioned turbines during the quarter. No injuries were reported, the other turbines continued operating and the affected units were covered by supplier warranties.

U.S. Rate Rise Triggers Impairment

Ørsted recorded a DKK 3.4 billion noncash impairment on its U.S. onshore and offshore projects. The accounting charge followed a 75-basis-point increase in long-dated U.S. interest rates during the quarter.

Quarterly Net Loss Reported

Net profit was negative DKK 700 million in the third quarter, despite the company’s stronger operating performance. The result was mainly affected by the noncash impairment, which more than offset higher EBITDA.

Return on Capital Declines

Adjusted return on capital employed fell to 7.4% from the prior-year level. Management attributed the decline to a larger capital base, even after excluding impairments and cancellation fees.

Net Debt Rises With Investment

Net debt reached DKK 38 billion at the end of the quarter, an increase of about DKK 16 billion. Gross investments were slightly above DKK 10 billion, reflecting continued spending on renewable construction projects.

Greater Changhua Sale Awaits Closing

The sale of a 55% stake in Greater Changhua 2 remains pending and is expected to close around year-end after final commissioning. Ørsted expects the transaction to reduce net debt by approximately DKK 25 billion once completed.

Sunrise Wind Tax Equity Not Signed

The Sunrise Wind tax-equity process was progressing, but equity investors had not signed agreements at the time of the call. The unresolved step remains a notable execution item for the project’s financing plan.

European Onshore Divestment Weighs on Earnings

The improvement in onshore earnings was partly offset by lower contributions after Ørsted sold its European onshore business earlier in the year. The divestment reduced the earnings base even as the remaining U.S. onshore operations performed well.

Guidance Remains Intact

Ørsted maintained 2026 EBITDA guidance of more than DKK 28 billion, excluding new partnerships and cancellation fees. Gross investment guidance was reduced by DKK 5 billion to DKK 45 billion-DKK 50 billion because of payment timing, while total project investment expectations were unchanged.

Projects and Auctions Set the Path Ahead

Ørsted expects full commissioning of Greater Changhua 2b and 4 in the fourth quarter, Sunrise Wind in the second half of 2027 and Blackwater Solar in the second half of 2027. Management also expects more than 15 gigawatts of auctions in 2027 and continues to target a 150-to-300-basis-point spread to WACC.

Ørsted’s call showed a business gaining momentum operationally, with stronger earnings and major offshore projects advancing. However, the impairment, higher leverage, safety concerns and pending transactions underline the execution risks investors must continue to monitor.

data.title: Asseco Poland Earnings Call Highlights Strong Growth
data.description:
Asseco Poland SA ((PL:ACP)) has held its Q3 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

Asseco Poland’s Earnings Call Signals Broad-Based Growth

The earnings call was strongly positive, with revenue, operating profit and net profit all posting double-digit gains in the first nine months of 2026. Management highlighted stronger margins, cash generation, acquisitions and a solid backlog, while cautioning that recovery-plan support and foreign-exchange gains may not be repeated at the same scale.

Revenue Growth Accelerates

Asseco Group generated PLN 14.206 billion in revenue during the first nine months of 2026, up 16% year over year. The increase points to broad demand for the group’s software and technology services across its main markets.

Profit Growth Outpaced Sales

Operating profit rose nearly 40% to almost PLN 1.7 billion, while net profit exceeded PLN 650 million after increasing 45%. The faster rise in earnings reflected stronger margins and operational improvements across the group.

Non-IFRS Results Strengthen

EBITDA reached PLN 2.339 billion, while non-IFRS EBIT was PLN 1.912 billion and non-IFRS net profit reached PLN 727 million. Non-IFRS EBIT from continuing operations grew more than 30%, with profitability improving by two percentage points.

Every Product Group Delivered Growth

All product groups recorded double-digit expansion in the first nine months. Public institution solutions grew 26%, ERP 18%, other IT solutions 15%, infrastructure and other products 11%, and financial solutions about 10%.

Public Institutions Lead Expansion

Public institution solutions generated PLN 3.756 billion in revenue, approximately 26% more than a year earlier. Growth exceeded 20% in each of the three geographic segments, while Poland increased 25% and passed PLN 1.1 billion in revenue.

Health Care Has an Exceptional Year

The health-care business performed particularly strongly, supported by projects linked to the National Recovery Plan. Asseco and its hospital customers delivered work on accelerated schedules, boosting both revenue and operating profit.

International Public Sector Gains Momentum

Asseco International’s public institution revenue rose about 21% to PLN 454 million. Government projects in Asseco Central Europe grew approximately 40% and were also described as performing well in terms of profitability.

Formula Systems Benefits From Israel Projects

Formula Systems generated PLN 2.2 billion in public institution revenue, up 27%. Matrix was the main contributor, driven by projects for public institutions in Israel.

Segments Post Solid Advances

Formula Systems revenue increased 20%, although roughly 30% of that growth came from foreign-exchange movements. Asseco International grew 7%, while Asseco Poland expanded 15% without an exchange-rate contribution.

Banking Remains a Key Strength

Financial solutions generated more than PLN 3 billion in revenue and grew about 10% across the group. Poland’s business increased 12% to PLN 544 million, while more than 40% of financial-market revenue came from recurring service and maintenance work.

Capital Markets Systems Reach Key Milestone

The group is rolling out its PROMAK NEXT solution and adapting brokerage systems to the Warsaw Stock Exchange’s new trading platform. Management said these projects reached a culmination during 2026.

ERP Expansion Continues

ERP solutions generated more than PLN 1.4 billion in revenue, up 18% across the group. Asseco International contributed PLN 863 million, up 12%, while Formula Systems rose 27% to PLN 569 million; the division has grown at a 13% compound annual rate over three years.

Formula Systems Shows Organic Growth

Formula Systems achieved 11% organic revenue growth after adjusting for foreign-exchange volatility. The result indicates that the segment’s expansion was supported by underlying demand, not only currency movements.

Margins Improve Across Operations

Profitability improved across the group as market conditions supported a better sales mix and operational efficiencies. Modern production tools and the restructuring of loss-making contracts in Central Europe also helped lift margins.

Key Subsidiaries Add to Results

Asseco Poland reported more than PLN 1.5 billion in revenue and PLN 377 million in operating profit, while Asseco Data Systems improved profitability. Asseco Cloud, ComCERT, Matrix IT and ACE Group also made positive contributions across public institutions, banking and international markets.

Cash Conversion Exceeds 100%

Cash conversion over the last 12 months exceeded 100%, and the group rebuilt its cash position in the third quarter after a weaker second quarter. Management said the year-end cash position was also expected to be strong.

Free Cash Flow Remains Robust

On a proportional-recognition basis, free cash flow reached PLN 1.2 billion in the first nine months. Cash conversion of EBIT was an especially strong 192%, underscoring the group’s ability to turn reported earnings into cash.

Acquisition Program Continues

Ten companies joined the group during or around the reporting period, including Poland’s McComp and Formula Systems’ Mexicano or Meckano and Laor Energy. Management continues to review the market and remains ready to complete further acquisitions.

Backlog Builds Toward 2027

Management reported dynamic backlog development extending into 2027. At fixed exchange rates, backlog was growing fastest at Asseco Poland, while the ranking between Asseco International and Formula Systems varied when currency movements were included.

Core Market Trends Remain Supportive

Management said current market trends remain favorable and that organic growth close to the average of the past three years could be achievable. It also noted that one-off factors may influence individual reporting periods.

Digitalization Creates New Demand

Companies and public institutions continue to invest in digital services, cloud computing and cybersecurity. Asseco is developing proprietary software and cloud capabilities while pursuing opportunities in local cloud initiatives and artificial intelligence.

ABS Sees Recurring-Business Potential

Management described ABS as structurally well positioned to turn market trends into recurring revenue. Its work on Poland’s national invoicing system, international sales and artificial-intelligence initiatives were identified as important areas of opportunity.

Cash Put to Work Efficiently

After the balance-sheet date, the group purchased PLN 100 million of corporate bonds fully backed by a bank. The investment was intended to provide a higher return than standard deposits while preserving funds for a future dividend.

Proprietary Software Supports Positioning

Asseco emphasized its focus on software for enterprises and public administration, supported by sector expertise and proprietary products. Management sees the group as a strategic partner and an early participant in major digitization projects.

Recovery Plan Boost Will Moderate

Management said the National Recovery Plan was the largest one-off factor supporting second-quarter results. Its recurring component will continue, but at a lower level, while the health-care sector’s 2026 performance was described as exceptional.

Currency Gains Are Uncertain

Favorable exchange-rate movements, including the stronger U.S. dollar against the shekel, added more than PLN 500 million to revenue and over PLN 73 million to non-IFRS operating profit. Management stressed that currency movements are outside its control and should not be assumed in future planning.

Tax Rate Moves Higher

The effective tax rate increased, mainly because of developments in the second quarter. It was slightly higher again in the third quarter as the revenue mix changed and the group made less use of available tax concessions.

One-Off CEO Award Raises Costs

The PLN 31 million year-over-year increase in management and overhead expenses included a PLN 25 million one-off Supervisory Board award to CEO Adam Góral. The total cost was higher after taxation, but management said the expense had already been paid and would not recur in coming quarters.

Long-Term Incentive Goal Is Ambitious

Management described the PLN 840 million net-profit target under its incentive program through 2030 as ambitious but reasonable. It also cautioned that 2026 earnings benefited from both the recovery-plan boost and foreign-exchange differences.

Legacy Contract Losses Ease

The prior year included loss-making contracts, mainly in Asseco International’s Central Europe operations. Some of those contracts have since been restructured, although cost pressure remains in areas outside salaries and employee benefits.

Outlook Points to Continued Momentum

Management said current trends should be sustained, while noting that the recurring part of the recovery-plan effect will be smaller. The public-sector backlog for the first quarter of 2027 was described as solid, with no material deterioration expected, and organic growth near the three-year average viewed as achievable; 2026 was called a record year, without assuming currency gains or the recovery-plan boost.

The call presented Asseco Poland as a company benefiting from broad demand, stronger profitability and disciplined cash generation. Investors will nevertheless need to separate durable organic growth from temporary support provided by the recovery plan and foreign exchange as the group advances its acquisition and digitalization strategy.
